page: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v6 is a general-purpose, low-memory variant cloud instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs spanning 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a clock frequency of 3.7 GHz. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 are present. The instance does not include a discrete GPU accelerator, but bundles 3,780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark outcomes show high multi-threaded compute capability, highlighted by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 22,158.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 98,458.65. Single-core performance is robust, with Geekbench recording 2,097.0 and stress-ng reaching 3,079.97. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 151.26 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth measures 103.51 GB/sec. Parallel processing capacity is further demonstrated by a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 391.6 GB/sec.

Data serving and computational benchmarks reflect the strength of the dedicated 64-vCPU topology. The server delivers 88.46 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and achieves a static web serving throughput of 47.36 GB/sec. In lightweight machine learning scenarios, the server registers 3,962.73 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M parameter LLM, falling to 15.99 tokens per second for a 70B parameter model.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the 2.0 GB per core memory density. Although designated in the general-purpose family, the 1:2 compute-to-memory profile functions like a compute-optimized tier. Compute density per dollar is advantageous for CPU-bound tasks, provided memory requirements remain moderate. The integrated 3,780 GB NVMe SSD suits high-throughput local disk needs. The instance fits code compilation, batch processing, static web serving, high-concurrency caching tiers, and general-purpose compute pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v6 is a compute-dense, low-memory virtual machine featuring an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 128.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), and a bundled 3,780 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPU hardware. Instruction sets include AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. Benchmark results show high-level multi-threaded CPU output, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,158.0 and 88.46 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside 47.36 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Because memory allocation is constrained to 2.0 GB per vCPU, this instance trades deep memory capacity for cost-efficient multi-threaded compute and local disk density. It is well-suited for code compilation, high-throughput caching, web servers, and distributed data processing workloads.
